The issue is that `ChatMessage` currently reads `agentSeed` by matching the item's author ID against available agents, but for helper threads the author is the parent agent (like Bubbles) rather than the helper itself (like Copy). Jamel wants the helper's name and mark to be used instead. I'm weighing two approaches: either add a helper field directly to `ThreadItem` so `ChatMessage` can render the `SubagentMark` when present, or have `buildThread` accept an optional identity override that applies the helper name and mark to all agent-authored items in that thread. The second option feels cleaner since it's a single configuration point, and only `SubagentRun` would need to pass this override. But there's a subtlety—the helper's thread also contains the person's own messages if they steer via the composer, and those should stay attributed to the person, not the helper. Only agent-authored items like replies, thinking, and tool calls should get the helper identity, while note items stay as crew.

Keeping it simple might mean not wrapping it in `MemberName` when it's a helper.

Looking at the design rules, agents always render their deterministic generated pet icon, never an avatar. A helper is different and should get its own generated mark. So the approach is to add a `helperSeed` field to `ThreadItem`, and when it's set, `ChatMessage` draws the helper mark instead of the agent icon, with the name rendered plain text rather than wrapped in `MemberName`. The `-ml-2` negative margin shifts it left by 8px, but that doesn't solve the core issue: if the button's minimum content width exceeds the available space after accounting for the padding, `max-width` won't force it to shrink below that minimum.

A block child with negative left margin inside a scroller creates an interesting situation: the scrollable overflow region doesn't include content overflowing on the start side (it just clips), but with `max-w-full` on the button, its max-width is 100% of the parent's content width, and starting at -8px means it extends further than expected.

I'm second-guessing whether I should've changed `openSubagent` to reuse the parent's tab instead of looking for an already-open tab showing that specific helper. The old behavior would find a tab with a matching threadId and bring it forward, or create a new one if needed—so opening different helpers would spawn separate tabs. But now I'm not sure if that's the right approach based on what I documented in AGENTS.md about tabs being closable and allowing multiple instances.

There's a real design tension here: `showSubagents` reuses tabs by `parentThreadId`, and the back button in the panel converts a helper tab back into the list by clearing the threadId. So the tab already operates as "one tab per parent thread, navigating between list and helper views." Under my old code, opening a second helper while one was open would create a second tab with the same parentThreadId, which `showSubagents` would then find inconsistently. My change makes this coherent—one helpers tab per thread, navigating between the list and whichever helper is active, matching the panel's two-screen design and the toggle button I'm adding. But I'm losing the ability to have several helpers open at once, and I'm not sure if that's a regression the user would actually notice or care about.

With chips in the thread, clicking helper A then helper B just replaces the view rather than opening two tabs side by side. You can't watch two at once anyway since there's only one panel. Tabs let you flip between them, but the list screen does that in one press. I think one tab per thread is simpler and makes the header toggle honest, but it does change behavior beyond what was asked. The safer approach would be to keep the "one tab per helper" behavior but record the parent so the toggle can find it—but then `closeSubagents` becomes ambiguous if there are several tabs. A toggle whose "off" state is unclear isn't simple. Maybe the button shouldn't be a toggle at all; the plan and board buttons toggle because those are pinned singular tabs, but helpers is just an ordinary tab. A simpler behavior might be to have the button just open the helpers tab rather than toggle it. I need to verify that closing tabs works correctly and that `closeSubagents` does what I expect. Jamel wants to replace the dedicated plan and other buttons with this single toggle, then let users add helpers, boards, and other items via a plus button in the panel, similar to how Codex handles an empty browser state.

I need to rethink the state model here — right now the panel only exists when tabs exist, but I should make `open` an explicit boolean flag that gets set true when any tab opens and false on closeAll, so the SidePanel can read directly from that state rather than inferring visibility from tab count.

The tricky part is handling cases like `hidePlan` where the app removes a tab as you navigate away from a thread — if that empties the tabs but you never explicitly opened the panel, it shouldn't stay open showing an empty landing page. So the rule should be: `open` becomes true when you ask for it or when a tab opens, and it becomes false when the app removes the last tab (since that's the app taking action, not you closing anything).

Actually, looking at the Codex screenshot, the panel stays open on the landing page even after the last tab closes — that's the desired behavior. So `open` should be its own independent flag: it turns true when the button is pressed or when a tab opens, and only turns false when you press the button again or click the close X. Closing the last tab leaves the panel open on the landing page, which matches what Codex shows and makes the landing page actually reachable.

But there's a problem with `hidePlan` and `hideWork` — they remove tabs automatically without user action. If one of those removes the only tab in the panel, you're left with an empty shell showing the landing rows, which feels wrong. The honest rule is: if hiding a tab leaves nothing behind, the panel should close too. I'll write that as a helper in the store so the logic lives in one place.

Now for `closeTab` when it's the last tab — that's different because you're closing it intentionally. Leaving the landing visible makes sense there, you're still in the panel but with nothing open. The X button in the header currently does `closeAll`, but with the panel having its own open state, it should just close the panel entirely. The header should always have the X button available as the way out, not just when there are tabs. Build a temp dir with `index.html`, a `main.tsx` that stubs `useCrew.setState({...})`
and renders the component at a fixed size, and a `probe.css`. **The css must be**

```css
@import "<repo>/src/renderer/src/styles.css";
@source "<repo>/src/renderer/src";
```

**Why:** Tailwind v4 detects content from the vite root. Importing `styles.css`
directly from a probe outside the repo compiles only the classes used in the probe
file itself, so the component renders completely unstyled and looks broken for a
reason that has nothing to do with the component. `@source` points the scan back at
the real tree.

**How to apply:** Put the probe under `node_modules/.<name>/` so nothing lands in
the auto-committing tree, `npx vite build --config <probe>/vite.config.ts`, then an
Electron main that `loadFile`s the built `dist/index.html`, waits ~1s and writes
`capturePage().toPNG()`. Delete the probe afterwards. Same shape as
`scripts/cover-sheet.mjs`, which is the committed version of this trick.

The vite config needs `base: './'`. Without it the built html asks for
`/assets/index.js`, which under `file://` is the disk root, so the page loads,
`did-finish-load` fires, nothing throws, and the capture is a black rectangle.
Check `document.getElementById('root').innerHTML.length` before believing a blank
shot. To see a `:hover` state, `webContents.insertCSS` the state on before capture,
since nothing can hover a headless window.
